suggestion.problemOrOpportunity: The actor board's host collection forks one resume status process per work order and spends about eleven git spawns per release tag. At current counts the operator's board takes about 19 s, and the document gate's critical path is about 20 s. Both grow by roughly a second a day as orders and releases arrive. The deferred register row for this cost names this exact reopen observation (above ten seconds). The same path has already failed full gates under load, and that was answered with a deadline change.
suggestion.scope: Give resume status a single-process form that returns every order's full status from one fold. Have release list cache per-tag results keyed by immutable tag object id; the recorded snapshot rule already treats tags as immutable evidence. collectSources then calls each once. Board output stays byte-identical, checked by the existing [document] test. A spawn-count test holds the process count constant with respect to order and tag counts.
evidenceRefs: npm run test:docs timing rows (console-docs 20.06 s of 24.81 s)
scratch tag-prefix drill: 1481/3035/4396/5627 ms at 24/47/70/93 tags
affectedUsers: the operator watching the actor board

suggestion.expectedValue: Roughly 17-18 s off each board render and off the document gate at current counts (the gate moves from about 25 s toward about 7 s). The saving grows by about a second a day as orders and releases accrue, and the growth that previously produced gate failures under load is removed.
suggestion.uncertainty: The estimate assumes a batched fold costs about one process start; the per-order call is 0.12 s, mostly start-up. The per-tag work in release list was profiled only by spawn count, so the cache's saving is inferred from the linear drill. Load behaviour inside the full gate was not re-measured.
risks: A batched status mode must reproduce each per-order status byte for byte, including attestation and legal next actions
A tag-keyed cache must be invalidated if the recorded tag-object snapshot rule changes
The console output is a product surface; the [document] test must remain its guard
alternatives: Run the per-order forks in parallel (lower latency, same linear process count)
Scale the per-command deadline again (the WO-128 route; a parameter that leaves the growth in place)
Move the host-collection test from test:docs to the review gate (moves the cost rather than removing it)
